en.headline: Police say white powder in letters to media and library poses no blast risk
en.dek: Four reports of letters containing white powder sent to three media outlets and a public library were classified as the discovery of suspicious items after checks found no explosive danger.
body: Hong Kong police said on Friday that four letters containing white powder received by three media outlets and one public library between 20 and 22 October posed no explosive danger after examination by the Explosive Ordnance Disposal Bureau.

The cases involved Yau Ma Tei Public Library, where staff found a suspicious letter in an accessible toilet on Tuesday, and the editorial offices of HK01, Dot Dot News under the Hong Kong Ta Kung Wen Wei Media Group, and Orange News. Some of the letters were sent by airmail from the United Kingdom and described as tip-offs from overseas readers.

Police said officers responded to each report, specialists examined the powder and removed it for further testing. Preliminary inquiries classified the cases as the discovery of suspicious items. No injuries were reported.
The Leisure and Cultural Services Department, which manages public libraries, said the letter at Yau Ma Tei Public Library was confirmed to pose no danger after police inspection.

zh.headline: 警方指傳媒及圖書館粉末信無爆炸危險
zh.dek: 三間傳媒機構及一間公共圖書館接獲藏有白色粉末的信件，經爆炸品處理課檢查後相信無爆炸危險，案件暫列發現可疑物品。
body: 警方周五表示，10月20日至22日接獲四宗報案，指有圖書館及傳媒機構收到載有白色粉末的信件，經爆炸品處理課人員檢查後，相信粉末沒有爆炸危險，並已檢走作進一步檢驗。
涉事地點包括油麻地公共圖書館，職員周二在傷殘人士廁所發現可疑信件；以及《香港01》、《點新聞》及《橙新聞》的編輯部。部分信件由英國空郵寄出，信封寫明是海外讀者報料。
警方稱人員到場處理，專家檢查後將粉末檢走。初步調查將案件列作「發現可疑物品」。事件無人受傷。
負責管理公共圖書館的康樂及文化事務署表示，油麻地公共圖書館的可疑郵件經警方檢查後確認沒有危險性。
